Google Research unveiled TurboQuant on March 24, 2026 as a compression algorithm for high-dimensional vectors, aimed, among other things, at alleviating bottlenecks in the KV cache of language models. According to the company, testing showed that it could reduce the size of this memory by at least 6 times, quantize the KV cache down to 3 bits without additional training or accuracy loss in benchmarking, and speed up the calculation of attention logits by up to 8 times compared to unquantized [...] What is TurboQuant, and what improvements does it offer?  
It’s an algorithm introduced by Google Research to compress high-dimensional vectors and reduce the size of the KV cache in AI models. In tests, Google claims it reduced memory by at least 6 times and quantized it to 3 bits without accuracy loss in the benchmarks used. [...] In fact, SK hynix has taken a completely different stance. results.title: TurboQuant: How Google Slashed the LLM KV Cache Bottleneck | AI2Work
results.content:
There's a real open question buried here. TurboQuant's compression is a substantially larger one-shot efficiency gain than DeepSeek achieved, and an independent analysis noted that most of the easy gains in KV-cache compression — int8, SmoothQuant, AWQ, sliding windows — are already deployed in production. The paper itself effectively marks a boundary: KV-cache compression is approaching its theoretical limit, and the next big inference win will have to come from a different direction entirely. [...] ## The Bigger Picture for AI Infrastructure

TurboQuant's authors — Google research scientist Amir Zandieh and VP/Google Fellow Vahab Mirrokni, with collaborators across Google DeepMind, KAIST, and NYU — built it on two prior works: QJL (AAAI 2025) and PolarQuant (AISTATS 2026). The TurboQuant paper itself was presented at ICLR 2026, making it a peer-reviewed contribution rather than a marketing claim. [...] 1TurboQuant compresses LLM KV caches from 16 bits to roughly 3-3.5 bits per value with near-zero accuracy loss, cutting inference memory by at least 6x.
 2On Nvidia H100 GPUs, 4-bit TurboQuant delivered up to an 8x speedup in computing attention logits versus an unquantized 32-bit baseline — a training-free, drop-in gain.

TurboQuant relies on two methods, PolarQuant and QJL, forming a two-stage pipeline to shrink memory while maintaining performance. According to Google, the technique targets the KV cache bottleneck and they plan to present at ICLR 2026.

results.title: Decoding the Jargon and Impact on Samsung, SK Hynix
results.content: To understand what TurboQuant is and what impact it may have, one must first decode the alien terminology. AI reads human language by breaking it into units called tokens — fragments of words. As a conversation grows longer, the AI temporarily writes down earlier tokens' context in memory such as HBM so it does not lose track. It is like sticking Post-it notes beside a thick book to remember the content. This temporary AI notepad is called the KV cache (Key-Value Cache). [...] It was a week in which global semiconductor stocks — particularly Korea's two memory chip giants Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK hynix (000660.KS) — were rocked by TurboQuant, an artificial intelligence compression technology unveiled by Google. Memory chipmakers' shares had been hitting record highs day after day on the back of surging demand. As the AI market shifted from training to inference, demand for not only high-bandwidth memory (HBM) but also DRAM and NAND flash grew [...] and NAND flash grew exponentially while supply remained tight. But the emergence of TurboQuant spread fears that "memory chips might sell less," sending related stocks tumbling in unison.
